Rosie Batty on QandA

To not talk about domestic violence...

I was part of an abusive relationship. Hope is the reason I didn't leave. Hope and low self esteem. My ex preyed on my insecurities, while simultaneously making me rely on him and him alone. Isolating me from family and friends not approved by him, and talking badly about me to the friends who were approved by him. He was an alcoholic and extremely violent. I was never one to back down, which lead to many nights in pain and crying while he got drunk. Through it all he told me no one else would ever love me. Which, having no other source of information, I believed. I "loved" him and hoped for change. He finally moved on and "cheated" on me. I put that in quotes, because now I realize that I was cheating myself the whole six years we were together. I'm so grateful to him for his infidelity. It was the catalyst I needed to get away. He's married to the girl he cheated on me with, and from what I can gather from her public FB profile, she's not much happier than I was.

Thank you for sharing your story. Really appreciate it.

Do you think that with the right help and social attitude you could have been in that relationship for a shorter period of time? Do you think that he could be educated to realise his actions were wrong and to change his ways? How do you feel about the fact that another woman is possibly going through what you went through with the same man?

I guess my main question is can this social problem be rectified with well placed resources or do you think a generational change is needed?

The idealist in me wants to believe with the right social programs in place I would have ended things sooner. However, I really believe that there is no way through the isolation. No one was allowed in or out without his say so, and the fear I had of him was real and profound. I have no idea what would have been effective against him.

The thing about abusers is they tend to be pretty charismatic. He convinced the world that he was a great guy and I was just a terrible wife, and was lucky that he put up with me. I spoke to his wife right after they got together, and told her what he was like. She didn't believe me. I was terrified to do this, but couldn't live with myself otherwise. She was convinced I was crazy, and just trying to get him back. I did what I could, but she was already gone.

There seems to be a lot of similarities with a woman I know... The isolation, the denigration and oddly the charismatic personality of the abuser. It makes me wonder what these people are exposed to when growing up for them to think that this is an acceptable form of relationship...

Rosie Batty has many good interviews published (along with other campaigners) exploring the issues. From the current conversation I think my take home message is this... We as a society must bring the scourge of domestic violence to the forefront of the public conscience. We need strong survivors to publicly talk about their experience (thankyou HeyRizzo) and we need to show current abusers, victims and children that this is not normal or acceptable.

Thanks again for sharing your story HeyRizzo and I would encourage you to tell it as many times as possible. Its a story that need to be heard.
